caption: The drawing shows a single object centrally positioned on a light-colored, plain background. The object appears to be an elongated metallic tool or device, primarily dark brown or black in color, consisting of a long, cylindrical rod extending horizontally from left to right. At the left end, the rod terminates in a flat, circular plate. Attached to the right end is a shaped metallic plate, with several pivoting components and three large hooked appendages hanging downward and to the right. One of the hooks extends directly downward, a second curves outward more steeply, and a third, smaller hook is attached at the top via a curled and looped connector. In the bottom left corner of the drawing, there is a small rectangular inset sketch showing a line-drawing version of the main object, including a scale marked “19” and simple outlines, but no additional detail. The only other markings visible are the artist’s signature and date at the lower right corner.
title: Iron Scales
